verdict.rationale: ByteAsk's headless `exec` mode can be dropped into scripts and CI pipelines, but it runs a single task and exits. Any schedule or trigger would come from the host CI platform, not from ByteAsk. The evidence shows no first-party always-on agents, recurring schedules, or event triggers for autonomous maintenance, and the docs stress approval before changes.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: For scripting and CI pipelines, use the `exec` subcommand
`byteask exec` - it runs one task to completion and exits.
